questions.q: Hardly had he reached the station ____ the train left.
questions.x: 'Hardly…when' and 'No sooner…than' are fixed pairs.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Not only the workers / but also the manager / was present at the meeting.
questions.x: The sentence is grammatically correct as written. Correct: with 'not only…but also', the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('manager').

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'A person who lends money at high interest'
questions.x: 'Usurer' means a person who lends money at high interest.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Vindicate'.
questions.x: 'Vindicate' means exonerate. 'Accuse' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'To eat humble pie' mean?
o: To admit a mistake and apologise
questions.x: 'To eat humble pie' means: to admit a mistake and apologise.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Hamper'.
questions.x: 'Hamper' is the opposite of 'Facilitate'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Hamper'.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'To take the bull by the horns' mean?
o: To deal with a problem directly and courageously
questions.x: 'To take the bull by the horns' means: to deal with a problem directly and courageously.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Ephemeral'.
questions.x: 'Ephemeral' is the opposite of 'Permanent'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Ephemeral'.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: SAGACIOUS
questions.x: 'Sagacious' means wise. 'Foolish' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: He is one of those officers who ____ always punctual.
questions.x: Correct answer: are. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'those officers' (plural).

questions.q: What example does the author give of activity that blunt survey questions may miss?
o: A woman tending livestock or helping in a family shop
questions.x: Answer: 'A woman tending livestock or helping in a family shop'. The passage gives this example. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Statistics are only as good as the questions behind them. A survey that asks whether a person 'worked' last week may miss a woman who spent hours tending livestock or helping in a family shop, because she does not think of this as work. Careful wording and trained interviewers reveal activity that blunt questions conceal. Policy built on incomplete data can misjudge both the problem and the solution.

questions.q: The central argument of the passage is that:
o: The design of survey questions shapes the quality of data and therefore of policy
questions.x: Answer: 'The design of survey questions shapes the quality of data and therefore of policy'. The opening and closing sentences make this point. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Statistics are only as good as the questions behind them. A survey that asks whether a person 'worked' last week may miss a woman who spent hours tending livestock or helping in a family shop, because she does not think of this as work. Careful wording and trained interviewers reveal activity that blunt questions conceal. Policy built on incomplete data can misjudge both the problem and the solution.

questions.q: The 1920 session of the Indian National Congress, presided over by C. Vijayaraghavachariar, was held at:
questions.x: It was held at Nagpur; it was the regular session that ratified the Non-Cooperation programme and reorganised Congress committees on linguistic lines.

questions.q: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the Chauri Chaura incident (1922) and Moplah rebellion?
questions.x: Lord Reading was Viceroy during the Chauri Chaura incident (1922) and Moplah rebellion.

questions.q: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856 was the result of efforts of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar. Lord Dalhousie drafted it; it was passed under Lord Canning.

questions.q:
In which year did the following take place?
The Swadeshi Movement was formally proclaimed at the Calcutta Town Hall meeting.
questions.x: The Swadeshi Movement was formally proclaimed at the Calcutta Town Hall meeting in 1905. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: Helena Blavatsky and Henry Olcott is associated with the founding of:
questions.x: Helena Blavatsky and Henry Olcott founded the Theosophical Society headquarters at Adyar (1882).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the RIN mutiny of 1946:
1. It began in Bombay on HMIS Talwar.
2. The Congress and League leadership fully supported the mutineers' continuing the revolt.
3. Sardar Patel and Jinnah persuaded the ratings to surrender.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
The leadership did not encourage continuing the revolt; Patel and Jinnah advised surrender.

questions.q: The Montagu Declaration of August 1917 announced the British goal as:
o: Progressive realisation of responsible government in India
questions.x: Correct answer: Progressive realisation of responsible government in India. It paved the way for the 1919 Act.

questions.q: The 'Akali movement' (Gurdwara Reform Movement) of the 1920s aimed to:
o: Free Sikh gurdwaras from corrupt mahants
questions.x: Correct answer: Free Sikh gurdwaras from corrupt mahants. It led to the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925 and the SGPC.

questions.q: Which newspaper/journal was published by Gandhi in South Africa?
questions.x: Indian Opinion was started in 1903.

questions.q: Arrange in chronological order: 1. Wood's Despatch 2. Hunter Commission on education 3. Raleigh Commission 4. Sadler Commission
questions.x: Correct answer: 1, 2, 3, 4. Wood's Despatch (1854), Hunter (1882), Raleigh (1902), Sadler (1917).

questions.q: The military exercise 'Harimau Shakti' is conducted between India and:
questions.x: 'Harimau Shakti' is a bilateral exercise between India and Malaysia.

questions.q: Anura Kumara Dissanayake became President of which country in September 2024?
questions.x: Correct answer: Sri Lanka. He leads the National People's Power coalition.

questions.q: The 'ULLAS' literacy programme targets adults aged:
questions.x: Correct answer: 15 years and above. It covers foundational literacy, numeracy and critical life skills.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of mission and objective:
1. Aditya-L1 — study of the Sun
2. NISAR — Earth observation
3. SpaDeX — docking demonstration
4. Gaganyaan — Mars orbiter
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Gaganyaan is the human spaceflight programme; Mangalyaan was the Mars orbiter.

questions.q: The 'Global Peace Index' is published by:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
questions.x: 'Global Peace Index' is brought out by Institute for Economics and Peace.

questions.q: Kisan Diwas (Chaudhary Charan Singh) is observed on:
questions.x: Kisan Diwas (Chaudhary Charan Singh): 23 December.

questions.q: 'Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) 2.0' aims to make cities:
questions.x: Correct answer: Garbage free. It focuses on source segregation and legacy waste remediation.

questions.q: 'Khelo India' is a scheme for:
o: Mass participation and promotion of sporting excellence
questions.x: Correct answer: Mass participation and promotion of sporting excellence. It includes Khelo India Youth Games and University Games.

questions.q: Which of the following organisations is headquartered in Addis Ababa?
questions.x: African Union is based in Addis Ababa.

questions.q: The landing point of Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander was named:
questions.x: Correct answer: Shiv Shakti point. The Chandrayaan-2 crash site was named Tiranga point.

questions.q: The President nominates how many members to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.x: They are persons with special knowledge in literature, science, art and social service.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Power of Parliament to legislate for two or more States by consent"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 252.

questions.q: Article 93 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People
Promotion of international peace and security
Supreme Court to be a court of record
Special leave to appeal by the Supreme Court
questions.x: Article 93: Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People.

questions.q: The national song 'Vande Mataram' is taken from which work?
o: Bharat Bharati by Maithili Sharan Gupt
questions.x: Correct answer: Anandamath by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay. 2025 marked 150 years of the song (composed in 1875).

questions.q: Who was the constitutional advisor to the Constituent Assembly?
questions.x: Sir B. N. Rau prepared the initial draft of the Constitution.

questions.q: The Constitution (71st Amendment) Act, 1992:
o: Gave effect to the India–Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement (exchange of enclaves)
Included Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali in the Eighth Schedule
Extended SC/ST reservation in legislatures and ended nomination of Anglo-Indian members
Limited the size of the Council of Ministers to 15% of the strength of the Lok Sabha/Assembly
questions.x: The 71st Amendment (1992) included Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali in the Eighth Schedule.

questions.q: Judicial review in India flows from all of the following Articles EXCEPT:
questions.x: Judicial review flows from Articles 13, 32, 226 and others and is part of the basic structure; Article 123 is the President's ordinance power.

questions.q: In S. R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Imposition of President's Rule is subject to judicial review and majority must be tested on the floor of the House
States have the right to secede
questions.x: Correct answer: Imposition of President's Rule is subject to judicial review and majority must be tested on the floor of the House. It also held secularism to be part of the basic structure.

questions.q: In February 2024, a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court struck down which scheme as unconstitutional?
questions.x: In ADR v. Union of India, the Court held the anonymous electoral bonds scheme violated the voters' right to information.

questions.q: The Central Bureau of Investigation derives its legal powers from the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946. The CBI was set up by a Home Ministry resolution in 1963.

questions.q: Which committee/body is associated with "Methodology for estimating poverty"?
questions.x: Suresh Tendulkar Committee (2009) dealt with methodology for estimating poverty.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Rise in repo rate
2. Sale of government securities by RBI
3. Reduction in CRR
4. Increase in SLR
How many of the above tend to reduce liquidity in the banking system?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Raising repo, OMO sales and raising SLR reduce liquidity; reducing CRR increases it.

questions.q: The 'Account Aggregator' framework regulated by the RBI enables:
o: Consent-based sharing of financial data across institutions
questions.x: Correct answer: Consent-based sharing of financial data across institutions. Account aggregators are NBFCs that act as consent managers.

questions.q: The FRBM Act was enacted in 2003 to:
o: Ensure fiscal discipline by setting deficit and debt targets
questions.x: It has been amended several times; the N. K. Singh Committee reviewed it in 2017.

questions.q: FEMA replaced FERA, marking a shift from:
o: Regulating and controlling to facilitating and managing foreign exchange
questions.x: Correct answer: Regulating and controlling to facilitating and managing foreign exchange. Violations under FEMA are civil, not criminal.

questions.q: 'Gig economy' expansion and 'formalisation' of the workforce are often tracked in India using:
o: EPFO payroll data and e-Shram registrations
questions.x: Correct answer: EPFO payroll data and e-Shram registrations. Payroll data proxies formal jobs; e-Shram covers unorganised workers.

questions.q: Nominal GDP of a country is ₹2,84,700 crore and real GDP (at base-year prices) is ₹2,19,000 crore. The GDP deflator is:
questions.x:
GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100 = (2,84,700 / 2,19,000) × 100 = 130.
Prices have risen 30% over the base year.

questions.q: In 2019–20, ten public sector banks were merged into four. Which bank was the anchor for the merger of Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India?
questions.x: Syndicate Bank merged with Canara Bank; Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank with Union Bank; Allahabad Bank with Indian Bank.

questions.q: SIDBI is the principal financial institution for:
questions.x: Correct answer: Micro, small and medium enterprises. Export-Import Bank of India finances foreign trade.

questions.q: If the CPI rises from 150 to 162 and a worker's wage rises from ₹20,000 to ₹22,000, the change in real wage is about:
Which error does NOT affect the agreement of the trial balance?
o: Wrong totalling of the purchases book
Omitting one side of an entry
questions.x: Errors of principle, complete omission, compensating errors and errors of commission in the right amount on the correct side leave the trial balance in agreement.

questions.q: A 'folio' column in the journal is used to record:
o: The page number of the ledger where the entry is posted
questions.x: Correct answer: The page number of the ledger where the entry is posted. Ledger folio (L.F.) helps cross-reference.

questions.q: When a provision for depreciation (accumulated depreciation) account is maintained, the asset account shows:
o: The asset at written down value
questions.x: Accumulated depreciation is shown as a deduction in the balance sheet.

questions.q: A firm has Cash ₹25,000, Debtors ₹75,000, Inventory ₹65,000, Prepaid expenses ₹5,000, Creditors ₹45,000, Bills payable ₹10,000 and Outstanding expenses ₹7,500. Its quick (acid-test) ratio is:
questions.x:
Quick assets exclude inventory and prepaid expenses: 25,000 + 75,000 = ₹1,00,000.
Current liabilities = ₹62,500.
Quick ratio = 1,00,000 / 62,500 = 1.6 : 1 (benchmark 1 : 1).

questions.q:
Match the subsidiary book with the transaction recorded in it:
Book:
A. Purchases book
B. Sales returns book
C. Bills payable book
D. Journal proper
Transaction:
1. Acceptances given to creditors
2. Credit purchase of furniture
3. Goods returned by customers
4. Credit purchase of goods
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Purchases book) → 4 (Credit purchase of goods); B (Sales returns book) → 3 (Goods returned by customers); C (Bills payable book) → 1 (Acceptances given to creditors); D (Journal proper) → 2 (Credit purchase of furniture).
Each subsidiary book records one class of transactions; residual entries go to the journal proper.

questions.q: Fixed costs are ₹1,96,000; selling price ₹275 and variable cost ₹240 per unit. How many units must be sold to earn a profit of ₹24,500?
questions.x:
Required units = (Fixed cost + Target profit) / Contribution per unit
= (1,96,000 + 24,500) / 35 = 6,300 units.

questions.q: Purchases during a month: 1st — 200 units @ ₹13; 10th — 200 units @ ₹15; 20th — 250 units @ ₹18. 600 units were issued on the 25th. Value of closing stock under FIFO is:
questions.x: Under FIFO the earliest units are issued first, so the 50 units left come from the latest purchases: 50 × ₹18 = ₹900.

questions.q: Opening inventory is ₹55,000, closing inventory is ₹1,00,000 and cost of goods sold for the year is ₹7,75,000. The inventory turnover ratio is:
questions.x:
Average inventory = (55,000 + 1,00,000) / 2 = ₹77,500.
Inventory turnover = COGS / Average inventory = 7,75,000 / 77,500 = 10 times.

questions.q: P and Q share profits in the ratio 4 : 1. They admit R for a 1/4 share, which R acquires from P and Q in their existing ratio. The new profit-sharing ratio of P, Q and R is:
A partner withdrew ₹1,000 at the middle of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 9% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 1,000 = ₹12,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the middle of each month = 6 months.
Interest = 12,000 × 9% × 6/12 = ₹540.

questions.q: Capital reserve, as distinct from revenue reserve, is generally created out of:
o: Capital profits (such as profit on reissue of forfeited shares)
questions.x: Correct answer: Capital profits (such as profit on reissue of forfeited shares). Capital reserves are not available for distribution as dividend.

questions.q: The rule in Garner v. Murray deals with:
o: Sharing the capital deficiency of an insolvent partner among solvent partners
questions.x: Solvent partners bear the deficiency in the ratio of their capitals just before dissolution (not profit ratio).

questions.q: A trader's capital at the beginning of the year was ₹70,000 and at the end ₹1,12,500. During the year he introduced fresh capital of ₹35,000 and withdrew ₹17,500 for personal use. His profit for the year is:
questions.x:
Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital
= 1,12,500 + 17,500 − 35,000 − 70,000 = ₹25,000 (statement of affairs method).

questions.q: Sale of an old fixed asset is a:
questions.x: Correct answer: Capital receipt. Any profit/loss on sale goes to the P&L account.

questions.q: Which ILO convention on labour inspection in industry and commerce has India ratified?
questions.x: India ratified C81, a governance convention; C129 concerns inspection in agriculture.

questions.q: Monthly remuneration is ₹30,000 of which basic + DA is ₹18,000 and the rest are excluded allowances. Under the 50% rule of the Code on Wages, 'wages' are:
questions.x: Excluded components = ₹12,000, which is below 50% of ₹30,000 (₹15,000), so no add-back; wages remain ₹18,000.

questions.q:
Match the central trade union organisation with its year of formation:
Organisation:
A. AITUC
B. INTUC
C. Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh
D. CITU
Year:
1. 1955
2. 1970
3. 1947
4. 1920
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (AITUC) → 4 (1920); B (INTUC) → 3 (1947); C (Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh) → 1 (1955); D (CITU) → 2 (1970).
AITUC 1920, INTUC 1947 (Congress-affiliated), BMS 1955 (Dattopant Thengadi), CITU 1970.

questions.q: Which method of verifying union membership for recognition purposes is generally considered most democratic?
questions.x: Secret ballot lets workers choose freely; the IR Code leaves the manner of verification to rules.

questions.q: The OSH Code provides for a free annual health check-up for employees of a specified age group. Under the central rules, this applies to employees aged:
questions.x: The Code provides annual free health examination for employees above a prescribed age (40 years under the draft central rules) in notified establishments.

questions.q: Under the IR Code, the Registrar may cancel the registration of a trade union if it has:
o: Wilfully contravened provisions of the Code or ceased to have the requisite membership
questions.x: Cancellation grounds include fraud, mistake, wilful contravention and fall in membership below the requirement.

questions.q:
Consider the following regarding the definition of 'industry' in the IR Code:
1. Domestic service is excluded.
2. Activities of government departments relating to defence research, atomic energy and space are excluded.
3. Hospitals run on a commercial basis are excluded.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The IR Code excludes domestic service, sovereign functions, charitable institutions and defence/atomic energy/space activities of government. Commercially run hospitals remain an 'industry'.

questions.q: In Hussainbhai v. Alath Factory Thozhilali Union (1978), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Trade unions cannot represent contract workers
Factory owners are not liable for any wages
Where the real employer is the factory owner, interposition of contractors does not defeat the workers' claim
questions.x: Looking beyond the veil, the Court held the factory owner to be the real employer of workers engaged through intermediaries.

questions.q: Section 11A, inserted into the Industrial Disputes Act in 1971, empowered Labour Courts and Tribunals to:
o: Set aside or modify the punishment of discharge or dismissal
Declare a strike illegal without hearing
questions.x: Section 11A gave adjudicators power to re-appreciate evidence and substitute a lesser punishment — a power retained in the IR Code.

questions.q: The 'Halsey' and 'Rowan' plans are examples of:
o: Incentive wage schemes sharing the time saved between employer and worker
questions.x: Halsey pays a share (often 50%) of time saved; Rowan pays a bonus proportional to time saved over standard time.

questions.q: In an establishment of 200 workers, Union X has 90 members, Union Y has 50 and Union Z has 30. Under the IR Code, the negotiating council will include:
questions.x: No union has 51%. X (45%) and Y (25%) cross the 20% threshold; Z has 15% and is left out.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Under the Code on Wages, the normal working day of an adult worker must ordinarily be fixed so that it does not exceed a prescribed number of hours.
Reason (R): Long working hours undermine the purpose of fixing a minimum time-rated wage.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. The appropriate government fixes the number of hours constituting a normal working day (rules prescribe a maximum, commonly 8 hours on a 48-hour week). This protects the value of a time-rated minimum wage.

questions.q: Which organisation compiles the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI), a major source of data on factory employment?
questions.x: ASI is conducted by NSO (MoSPI) covering factories registered under the Factories Act.

questions.q: The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) shares with employers a portion of the stipend payable to apprentices. NAPS is administered by the Ministry of:
questions.x: NAPS (2016) is under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; NATS for graduate apprentices is under the Ministry of Education.

questions.q: Which feature of the Labour Codes is aimed at reducing the compliance burden on employers through single-window processes?
o: Exemption of all MSMEs from every labour law
Replacing labour courts with civil courts
Single registration, single licence and single return for establishments
questions.x: The Codes provide for one registration, one licence and one return instead of separate filings under multiple Acts.

questions.q: The PENCIL portal, launched in 2017, is meant for:
o: Effective enforcement of the child labour law and the NCLP
questions.x: PENCiL (Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour) connects central, state and district governments, civil society and the public.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains 'exclusion error' in targeted social security programmes?
o: Eligible persons fail to receive the benefit
questions.x: Exclusion error leaves out the deserving; inclusion error covers the undeserving.

questions.q: Under the investment pattern notified for EPFO, the permissible investment in equity and equity-related instruments (largely ETFs) is:
questions.x: The Ministry of Labour's pattern allows 5–15% in equity, mostly through ETFs tracking Nifty/Sensex and CPSE/Bharat-22 ETFs.

questions.q: Under the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995, a member retires at 58 with pensionable salary of ₹10,000 and pensionable service of 18 years (including any weightage). The monthly member pension is:
questions.x:
Monthly pension = (Pensionable salary × Pensionable service) / 70
= (10,000 × 18) / 70 = ₹2,571.
Pensionable salary is the average of the last 60 months' wages (subject to the ₹15,000 ceiling), and the minimum pension is ₹1,000.

questions.q: EDLI benefit becomes payable to the nominee or family when:
o: The member dies while in service
questions.x: Correct answer: The member dies while in service. EDLI is a death-in-service insurance benefit.

questions.q: An establishment covered under the EPF & MP Act continues to be covered even if the number of employees later falls below 20. This principle is called:
questions.x: Section 1(5) provides that coverage continues even if employment falls below 20.

questions.q: The EPF interest rate of 8.10% declared for 2021–22 was notable because:
o: It was the lowest in about four decades
It was the first rate ever declared
questions.x: 8.10% was the lowest since 1977–78; rates later rose to 8.15% and 8.25%.

questions.q: An employee retires after 7 years and 8 months of continuous service. Last drawn monthly wages (basic + DA) are ₹29,000. Gratuity payable under the statutory formula (non-seasonal establishment) is:
questions.x:
Gratuity = 15/26 × last drawn wages × completed years of service.
8 months is more than six months, so it counts as a full year → 8 years.
= 15/26 × 29,000 × 8 = ₹1,33,846 (well within the ₹20 lakh ceiling).
The divisor 26 reflects working days in a month.

questions.q: A member with pensionable salary ₹15,000 and 21 years of pensionable service retires at 58. Including the 2-year weightage, the monthly EPS pension is:
questions.x: Pensionable service = 21 + 2 (weightage for 20+ years) = 23; pension = 15,000 × 23 / 70 ≈ ₹4,929.

questions.q: The 'three-pillar' pension model popularised by the World Bank (1994, 'Averting the Old Age Crisis') comprises:
o: A public mandatory pillar, a private mandatory funded pillar and voluntary savings
questions.x: The World Bank later expanded it to a five-pillar framework (adding a zero pillar of social assistance and non-financial support).

questions.q: Gratuity payable under the law can be attached in execution of a court decree?
o: No, it is protected from attachment
questions.x: Correct answer: No, it is protected from attachment. Statutory gratuity is exempt from attachment under any court decree.

questions.q: The ESI scheme provides enhanced sickness benefit at 100% of wages for:
questions.x: Enhanced sickness benefit at full wages is given for 7 days (vasectomy) or 14 days (tubectomy), extendable on medical advice.

questions.q: Under EPS 1995, if both parents of a child are dead, the orphan pension is payable to how many orphans at a time?
questions.x: Orphan pension (75% of widow pension) is paid to two orphans at a time until 25 years; disabled children lifelong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. RAM is volatile memory.
2. ROM retains data without power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Correct answer: Both 1 and 2. Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct.
Both are correct.

questions.q: The 'expiry date' on medicines matters because after it:
o: The drug's potency and safety are not assured
questions.x: Correct answer: The drug's potency and safety are not assured. Stability is guaranteed only up to the expiry date.

questions.q: The chemical name/formula of 'gypsum' is:
questions.x: Gypsum = CaSO₄·2H₂O (calcium sulphate dihydrate).

questions.q: The 'BCG' vaccine is given to protect against:
questions.x: Correct answer: Tuberculosis. It is given at birth in India.

questions.q: Hydroponics is the technique of growing plants:
o: Without soil, in nutrient-rich water solutions
questions.x: Correct answer: Without soil, in nutrient-rich water solutions. It is used in controlled-environment agriculture.

questions.q: Insulin (isolation) is credited to:
questions.x: Insulin (isolation): Frederick Banting and Charles Best.

questions.q: The octal number 17 is equal to decimal:
Photosynthesis takes place in which cell organelle?
questions.x: Correct answer: Chloroplast. Chlorophyll absorbs light energy.

questions.q: In computing, 'TCP' stands for:
questions.x: TCP = Transmission Control Protocol.

questions.q: The SI unit of magnetic flux density is the:
questions.x: Magnetic flux density is measured in Teslas.

questions.q: CNG used in vehicles is mainly:
questions.x: Correct answer: Methane. It burns more cleanly than petrol or diesel.

questions.q: 'Blockchain' technology is best described as:
questions.x: Correct answer: A decentralised, tamper-resistant distributed ledger. Cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin use blockchain.

questions.q: In a row, Pooja is 17th from the left and Rekha is 12th from the right. When they interchange their positions, Pooja becomes 23rd from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
questions.x:
After interchange, Pooja occupies Rekha's old place, which is 12th from the right and now 23rd from the left.
Total = 23 + 12 − 1 = 34.

questions.q: How many arrangements of the letters of 'LEDGER' are there in which the vowels are NOT all together?
questions.x:
Total arrangements = 360 (E appears 2 times).
Vowels together = 120 × 1 = 120.
Not all together = 360 − 120 = 240.

questions.q: An inspector drives from town P to town Q at 48 km/h and returns along the same road at 96 km/h. The average speed for the whole journey is:
questions.x:
For equal distances, average speed = 2uv/(u + v) (harmonic mean), not (u + v)/2.
= 2 × 48 × 96 / (48 + 96) = 9216/144 = 64 km/h.

questions.q: At simple interest a sum doubles itself in 12 years. In how many years will it become 3 times itself at the same rate?
questions.x:
Doubling means interest = 1 × principal in 12 years, i.e. rate = 100/12 = 8.33% p.a.
To become 3 times, interest must be 2 × principal.
Time = (2 × 100) / 8.33 = 24 years. (Rule: time ∝ number of times the principal is earned as interest.)

questions.q: The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 9 : 5. After 7 years, the ratio will become 25 : 17. What is P's present age?
A starts a business with ₹30,000. B joins after 5 months with ₹30,000, and C joins after 4 months with ₹15,000. Out of a year-end profit of ₹6,900, B's share is:
questions.x:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
A: 30,000×12, B: 30,000×7, C: 15,000×8 → 12 : 7 : 4.
B's share = 7/23 × 6,900 = ₹2,100.

questions.q: Find the volume of a cylindrical water tank of radius 14 m and height 26 m. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.x:
V = πr²h = (22/7) × 14 × 14 × 26 = 16016 m³.
(Curved surface 2πrh would be 2288 m² — a common mix-up.)

questions.q: An article is marked 60% above its cost. Two successive discounts of 10% and 10% are then given on the marked price. The resulting gain or loss per cent is:
questions.x:
Take CP = 100 → MP = 160.
After 10%: 144; after a further 10%: 129.6.
Net = 129.6 − 100 = 29.6 → 29.6% gain.
Successive discounts are multiplied, never added (10% + 10% ≠ 20%).

questions.q: ₹31,000 is invested for 1 year at 12% per annum, interest being compounded half-yearly. The compound interest earned is:
questions.x:
Half-yearly: rate per period = 12/2 = 6%, number of periods = 2.
Amount = 31,000 × (1 + 6/100)² = ₹34,831.60.
CI = ₹3,831.60 (slightly more than annual compounding, which gives ₹3,720).

questions.q:
Production of a fertiliser unit (thousand tonnes) — 2021: 255  |  2022: 295  |  2023: 295  |  2024: 275  |  2025: 255.
In which year was the percentage growth over the previous year the highest?
questions.x:
Year-on-year growth: 2022: 15.69%; 2023: 0%; 2024: -6.78%; 2025: -7.27%.
Highest growth: 2022 (15.69%). Note: the largest absolute rise need not be the largest percentage rise.

questions.q: On which day of the week did 14 November 1990 fall?
questions.x:
Odd-day method (Sunday = 0).
Completed years = 1989: 1600 years → 0 odd days; 300 years → 1; remaining 89 years have 22 leap + 67 ordinary → 22×2 + 67 = 111 → 6 odd day(s).
Days elapsed in 1990 up to 14 November = 318 → 3 odd day(s).
Total = 1 + 6 + 3 = 10 → 3 → Wednesday.

questions.q: A bag has 6 white and 5 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random together. What is the probability that at least one of them is white?
questions.x:
P(at least one white) = 1 − P(both black).
P(both black) = C(5,2)/C(11,2) = 10/55.
Required = 1 − 2/11 = 9/11.

questions.q: The average of 9 observations is 53. The average of the first 5 is 54 and that of the last 5 is 44. The 5th observation is:
questions.x:
Sum of all 9 = 9 × 53 = 477.
First 5 + last 5 = 5×54 + 5×44 = 490; the middle observation is counted twice.
Middle = 490 − 477 = 13.

questions.q: Farhan starts from point O and walks 9 km towards North, then turns right and walks 24 km, then turns right and walks 13 km, and finally turns right and walks 27 km. What is the shortest distance and direction of the final position from O?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: +9 -13 = -4 km → 4 km South.
East–West: +24 -27 = -3 km → 3 km West.
Distance = √(3² + 4²) = 5 km, towards South-West.
